German Body Parts: A1 Vocabulary Exercises

Learn Kopf, Hand, Fuß and Auge with articles and plural forms. Practise German body-part vocabulary in everyday, non-diagnostic example sentences.

A1 level4 worked examples4 practice questions

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Vocabulary and usage

Learn der Kopf (Köpfe), die Hand (Hände), der Fuß (Füße) and das Auge (Augen). Kopf is head, Hand is hand, Fuß is foot and Auge is eye. Three plurals change their vowel. Nouns for body parts are capitalised, just like other German nouns.

Common mistake to avoid

Do not assume that Fuß and Hand share a gender because both name body parts. Learn der Fuß and die Hand separately.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Notice each word’s meaning, article and common word partners in context.

Worked example 1Auf meinem Kopf sitzt ein warmer Hut.There is a warm hat on my head.
Worked example 2Sie hält die Karte in der linken Hand.She is holding the card in her left hand.
Worked example 3Der rechte Fuß passt gut in den Schuh.The right foot fits well in the shoe.
Worked example 4Das Kind schließt ein Auge.The child closes one eye.

Practice: choose the matching word

Choose the word from the bank that matches the English cue and sentence. Use each item once; keep its spelling and capitalisation. Try each question before opening the answer. A dash (—) means no word is needed. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Word bank: Auge · Fuß · Hand · Kopf

Question 1. Der Hut gehört auf den ___. (head)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: Kopf

Kopf names the head; auf den is used for the destination here.

Question 2. Ich winke mit der rechten ___. (hand)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: Hand

Hand is feminine; mit takes the dative article der.

Question 3. Am rechten ___ trage ich einen blauen Schuh. (foot)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: Fuß

Fuß is masculine; am is short for an dem.

Question 4. Ich sehe mit dem linken ___ durch das Loch. (eye)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: Auge

Auge is neuter, with dative dem after mit.

Revise it so it sticks

Return to this lesson tomorrow and complete the four gaps without looking at the rule. Then write two of your own sentences using today's pattern. Check whether the subject, case and verb position match the explanation.
